body.heading: Where in the world is Syria?
paragraphs: Syria is a country in Western Asia, which is part of Asia.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Syria is Damascus.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Syria is Arabic.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Syria is the Syrian pound.

body.heading: How big is Syria?
paragraphs: Syria covers about 185,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of Japan.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Damascus is one of the oldest continuously lived-in cities in the world. Its old city holds the great Umayyad Mosque and covered souqs smelling of spices and sweets.
Palmyra was a Silk Road oasis city of colonnaded streets and temples in the Syrian desert, once ruled by Queen Zenobia.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Syria on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Syria in one breath: a country in Western Asia, capital Damascus, where people speak Arabic and pay with the Syrian pound.
